questions.stem: In the Data vs Metadata discussion in *I Am Datapedia!*, what saying is attributed to Daniel Lundin?
options: Data without Metadata is a Data Swamp
One person's Metadata is Data for another person
Metadata should always be stored with the raw data
Raw data must be kept for life
Summarised data is never Metadata
questions.explanation: Daniel Lundin's remark that one person's Metadata is Data for another person frames the whole discussion.

questions.stem: In the Data vs Metadata argument, which kind of data is being referred to?
options: Raw Data coming from source systems into next datastores such as a Data Lake or Data Warehouse
Only reference data held in lookup tables
Only data that has already been summarised in a dashboard
Only structured data in relational tables
Only data produced by Metadata tools
questions.explanation: The discussion refers only to Raw Data arriving from source systems such as OLTP applications, social media or unstructured datasets into a Data Lake or Data Warehouse.

questions.stem: Which of the following is given as an example of an unstructured raw dataset?
options: A relational sales table
A KPI on a dashboard
A column name
Video, audio, PDF or email
A data dictionary
questions.explanation: Video, audio, PDF and email are the examples of unstructured datasets flowing from source systems.

questions.stem: What kind of data do decision makers normally look at, according to the Data vs Metadata argument?
options: Summarised data, which is transformed data and therefore Metadata
Every individual transaction row
Only operational log data
Only raw data from social media
Only column names and data types
questions.explanation: Decision makers normally look at summarised data, which is not actual data but transformed data, that is data about data, or Metadata.

questions.stem: Which figures does a decision maker want when deciding whether to reinvest in a product?
options: Every sale transaction of the product in each region
The database schema of the sales system
The raw social media posts about the product
The list of ETL jobs that load the sales data
TOTAL sales, TOTAL cost and other totals such as TOTAL marketing cost
questions.explanation: A decision maker deciding on reinvestment wants totals: total sales, total product cost and other expenses such as total marketing cost.

questions.stem: Roughly what percentage of occasions call for investigating transactional data, according to the Data vs Metadata argument?
options: About 50%
About 30%-40%
About 90%
Nearly 100%
About 5%-10%
questions.explanation: Investigation comes into the picture only when something is wrong, which is around 5%-10% of occasions.

questions.stem: Why do source systems normally not allow a lot of read hits?
options: Because they do not store raw data
Because they never want to compromise the performance of their systems
Because regulators forbid direct queries
Because Metadata cannot be extracted from them
Because they only store summarised data
questions.explanation: Source systems limit read hits mainly because they do not want to compromise their own performance.

questions.stem: Which development might remove the performance concern that limits read hits on source systems?
options: Storing more raw data in the Data Warehouse
Replacing Metadata with Master Data
Cloud with auto-scaling capability
Purging all Metadata after extraction
Moving all systems back on-premises
questions.explanation: The performance concern is true for on-premises infrastructure, but Cloud with auto-scaling capability may remove that challenge sooner or later.

questions.stem: What is the author's own view on whether raw transactional data still needs to be pulled and maintained in the next storage?
options: It must always be kept for life
It should be kept only in the source system's backup
It should be duplicated in every datastore
For the author there is no need, though time will tell
It should be kept only for unstructured data
questions.explanation: The author's position is that there is no need to pull and maintain raw transactional data, while acknowledging that time will tell.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a reason given for keeping raw data for a certain time?
options: Fulfilling regulatory requirements
Investigating when something is wrong
Improving the performance of the source system
Allowing decision makers to see transactional data
Extracting Metadata from it
questions.explanation: Regulatory needs, investigation, transactional views and Metadata extraction are all discussed; keeping raw data does not improve source system performance.
